hero.oneLiner: TANFAC transformed from a legacy HF producer to India’s sole solar-grade DHF manufacturer with a clear path to HFC-32 dominance, driven by record order books, 65% pre-sold downstream capacity, and aggressive capex — positioning it as the only Indian player with integrated fluorochemical value chain access to high-growth energy transition markets.
hero.industry: Fluorochemicals & Advanced Materials for Energy Transition

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- One of the market leaders in the domestic Hydrofluoric Acid market and among the largest producers of Anhydrous Hydrofluoric Acid (AHF) in India; the first and only supplier of Solar Grade Diluted Hydrofluoric Acid (DHF) in India.
- Joint sector company with TIDCO and Anupam Rasayan India Ltd; Anupam Rasayan acquired a joint stake in 2021-22, bringing fluorination chemistry expertise and helping EBITDA surpass its prior 2019 peak.
- 4 decades of fluorine chemistry track record since 1985, with 105+ clients across 10+ countries and established relationships with marquee customers and suppliers.
- Expansion of the product portfolio into high-value fluorine derivatives is positioned as an entry barrier for new entrants, as the company transitions from commodity chemicals to specialty solutions through forward integration.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: HF: 95% utilization; Sulphuric acid: 101% utilization; Specialty fluorides: 41% utilization (ramping); Solar DHF: 20k tpa capacity, INR15-20/kg premium over industrial HF; HFC-32: 20k tpa under construction, INR240-280/kg production cost, 75-80% export focus

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR1,068cr for solar grade DHF (executed over 3.5 years); INR3,612cr in long-term supplier agreements (5-7y); 13,000 tpa (65%) of 20k tpa HFC-32 capacity pre-contracted

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 25-30% CAGR over next 3 years; margin: 15-18% range-bound for existing business, >20% expected from HFC-32; order inflow: 80-85% of HFC-32 capacity pre-booked; capex/commissioning: INR495cr for HFC-32 plant (commissioning Q3 FY27), additional 30k tpa HF plant (announcement expected in 2-3 months), 20k tpa solar DHF expansion (targeting June 2027)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 20k tpa additional solar DHF capacity (targeting June 2027); 30k tpa HF expansion (to be announced); pipeline in electronic grade fluorinated chemicals, battery electrolytes, high-performance fluoropolymers, inorganic fluorides

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Industrial HF margin: ~INR10-15/kg lower than solar DHF; HFC-32 margin: significantly high (payback <4y); cost pressures: sulphur up from INR30/kg to INR38-40/kg; fluorspar stable; 100% cost pass-through achieved with 30-40 day lag

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for HFC-32 and solar DHF expansions; funding via mix of promoter equity (preferential allotment), QIP, and debt; no dividend payout mentioned — all cash flow reinvested in growth

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, assertive, and strategically focused — repeatedly emphasized execution capability, backward integration, and government support for Atmanirbhar Bharat; dismissed quota concerns by citing public office memorandum; projected 30%+ revenue CAGR with clear visibility

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: HFC-32 quota allocation uncertainty (though EC secured and government memorandum supports capacity-based allocation); raw material price volatility (sulphur); execution risk on multi-crore capex projects; regulatory delay in quota issuance beyond Jan 2028

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: TANFAC is the only Indian player with integrated HF → solar DHF → HFC-32 chain; 65% pre-sold HFC-32 capacity is unprecedented in Indian chemical sector; HF expansion is not included in INR495cr capex — implying additional INR300-400cr capex is imminent; solar DHF purity <10 PPB is a USFDA-CGMP level barrier to entry; 85% of solar DHF capacity already booked despite only 20k tpa production

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| India's HFC-32 quota allocation uncertainty | TANFAC INDUSTRIES LTD. | beneficiary | High | Only Indian player with EC, pre-sold contracts, and government memorandum support — poised to capture 15-20% of national quota despite no HCFC baseline |
| Global reliance on Chinese fluorochemicals for solar PV and refrigerants | TANFAC INDUSTRIES LTD. | beneficiary | High | Positioned as sole Indian source of solar DHF and HFC-32 — critical for India’s solar PV and AC manufacturing self-reliance under Atmanirbhar Bharat |
| High cost of fluoropolymer imports for electronics and batteries | TANFAC INDUSTRIES LTD. | beneficiary | Medium | R&D pipeline in electronic grade fluorinated chemicals and battery materials creates long-term arbitrage opportunity against imports |
| SRF, GFL, Navin lack downstream HFC-32 capacity | SRF LTD. | loser | Low | Incumbents have HCFC baselines but no announced HFC-32 capacity — TANFAC’s integrated, greenfield HFC-32 plant may capture first-mover advantage in domestic market |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Ownership] Promoter group comprises TIDCO (Tamil Nadu government entity) and Anupam Rasayan India Ltd, making TANFAC a joint-sector company.
- [Technology partners] Know-how and equipment sourced from Buss Chemtech (Davy Process), Switzerland, and Chenco, Germany; refrigerant gas tie-up with a Japanese company.
- [Leadership integration] CFO Mr. N. R. Ravichandran's listed contact email uses the anupamrasayan.com domain, reflecting close operational ties with promoter Anupam Rasayan.
